cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Come to the reunion with me. Let them see us arrive holding hands. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I know. I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep hold while I say it?

mechanism: A confidently organizes a public couple entrance but cedes pace and takes the first disclosure risk so B will demonstrate shared trust.
confusable: Unlike merely seeking attendance, A asks for visible relationship acknowledgment; borrowed authority depends on rebuilding cooperation after A previously let go.
comparison: Public reunion and handholding differ from private reciprocal disclosure through awkward messages.
seedUse: Use D80-a reunion/handholding/prior withdrawal and S02-b adapting the participation method while keeping a leader voice.
